Final pre-ship audit of GitHub PR #68 in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch `feature/SFCC-194_pdp-was-now-price` is checked out at `fd249e4` (final state). READ-ONLY — do not modify, stage, commit, or checkout.

YOUR SCOPE: **code quality, architecture, and structure.** Other agents cover requirements traceability, Figma conformance, and test integrity. Do not report on those.

## The change

11 source files, ~850 insertions. Full list:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/{index.tsx,zimmProductPrice.css.ts,index.test.tsx,index.stories.tsx}
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx}
overrides/app/pages/product-detail/{index.tsx,productInfo.ts,productInfo.test.ts,variantScopedPrice.ts,variantScopedPrice.test.ts,partials/staticProductHeader.tsx}
overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx
.claude/registry/*.md  (generated — ignore)
```

`variantScopedPrice.ts` is **new** (124 lines) — extracted mid-review from `product-detail/index.tsx`. Give it proportionate attention; it hasn't had a full quality read yet.

## Standards — read these first and treat them as the bar

- `.claude/rules/conventions.md` — cross-cutting (naming, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic numbers, comments, security)
- `.claude/rules/components.md` — component/hook structure, **Composition** section (complexity limits, container/presentational, extract-to-hook threshold), Storybook categorisation
- `.claude/rules/typescript.md` — `any`, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming
- `.claude/rules/css.md` + `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` — the styling hierarchy, `var(--zimm-*)` vs bare keys, units, component-local tokens, one-canonical-styling-surface, co-located `.css.ts` governance, the relative-vs-base-path import trap
- `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` / `frozenFiles.md` — tier of every file touched
- `AGENTS.md` — Rules section: Minimal changes, Comments, Icons, TypeScript-only-in-overrides

## What I want

1. **Architecture and layering.** Is the atom/molecule/mapper/page split correct and clean at final state? Does `variantScopedPrice.ts` sit at the right layer? Is `product-detail/index.tsx` genuinely better after the extraction, or did it just move? Check the container/presentational boundary holds — no data-fetching in components, with the documented `useIntl`/`useUiCopy` exception.
2. **`variantScopedPrice.ts` in depth.** Signature design, parameter order, naming, types, whether it's genuinely pure, JSDoc quality, and whether the ~20-line "this mechanism is unreachable" comment block it carries is appropriate or is documenting dead code that should simply be deleted. Form your own view on whether the dead code should still be there.
3. **Comment quality across the change.** This PR is unusually comment-dense. Assess: are the comments earning their keep, or is there over-documentation? Are any factually wrong *now* (several were rewritten during review — verify the current text against the current code)? Specifically check every comment that cites a `file:line` reference and confirm it still resolves — line-number pins rot, and this PR has moved a lot.
4. **TypeScript quality** at final state — including the `any` aliases in `product-detail/index.tsx` (`SfccProduct`, `SfccVariant` etc.), whether `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s types are honest, and any `as` casts.
5. **CSS/token structure** — the recipe's shape (parts, baseStyle covering all parts, variants), whether styling is fully in the recipe with none leaking to JSX, and tier/CODEOWNERS routing of every file touched.
6. **DRY/duplication** — is anything now duplicated between `productInfo.ts` and `variantScopedPrice.ts`, or between the page and the extracted module?
7. **Minimal-changes discipline** — anything in the diff unrelated to SFCC-194.

## Baseline facts (verified, don't re-derive)

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm run test` — 408 pass / 26 files
- `npm run lint` — 4 errors, 16 warnings. **All 4 errors are pre-existing** in `overrides/app/routes.tsx` and `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`, neither touched by this PR. Zero lint errors are attributable to this change.
- `npm run audit:tokens` — no new violations from this PR.
- `Storybook interaction & a11y tests` CI job is FAILING on the Was-price contrast (`#969696`, 2.96:1). Known, being handled separately — not your scope.

## Method — closed loop

- Open every file you cite. Never report from a diff or grep line alone.
- Compare against **sibling components that already exist** to establish what "the established approach" is in practice, not just what the docs say — cite the sibling you compared to (e.g. other `ui-kits/atoms/*`, `footer/*.css.ts`).
- Mark **CONFIRMED** vs **PLAUSIBLE**. Where a rule has a documented exception, check whether it applies before calling it a violation.
- Be fair. This code has been through two review rounds and is largely good. Do not manufacture findings to pad a list — a short list of real issues is worth more. If a dimension is clean, say so in one line.

## Output

Ranked findings: `file:line` — severity (Blocker / Major / Minor / Nit) — the issue in one sentence — the rule or sibling precedent it violates — CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE. Then a short section on what is genuinely well done. Then a three-line verdict on whether this is shippable on code-quality grounds. No preamble.

content.text:
## Ranked findings

**1. `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/variantScopedPrice.ts:60-82` vs `:99-114` — Major — the module's own unreachability argument, if true, makes the stale-pid cross-check directly above it inert, so the two comment blocks cannot both describe reality. CONFIRMED (static trace).**
Whenever `urlPid` is set, `requestedProductId` is that pid (`index.tsx:198`), so `product` is the standalone **variant**. If variant responses always carry `variants[]` — the premise of the unreachability block — then line 88 sets `masterProduct = product` (the variant), and `getPriceData` → `findLowestPrice` takes the `[product]` branch for non-masters (`product-utils.js:257`, verified) and **ignores the injected colour-filtered `variants`**. Result in the stale-pid scenario (`?color=white&pid=BLACK-MD`): the price returned is BLACK-MD's own — exactly the bug lines 101-111 say the guard prevents. `isPriceStale` (`index.tsx:365`) doesn't catch it either, because `requestedProductId === product.id`. The guard only works via `effectiveCachedMaster` — the path the header comment declares dead. `variantScopedPrice.test.ts:95` passes `masterWithAll` (a master) as `product` for the B4 case, a shape that cannot occur when `urlPid` is set, and `getPriceData` is mocked so the test cannot see the swallowed filter. Rule: conventions.md "no magic/unverified assumptions"; repo memory *Prove, don't assert*.

**2. `variantScopedPrice.ts:60-82` — Major — a 20-line block documenting live code the author believes never runs, now locked in by four unit tests (B7-B10). CONFIRMED.**
My view: it should not ship in this shape, but **deleting it is not the safe default either** — per finding #1 it is the only path that makes the stale-pid guard work. Resolve #1 first; the decision is binary. If the premise is verified true, delete the block, the `cachedMaster` param, `cachedMasterMatchesCurrent`, `effectiveCachedMaster`, the deep-link fallback, B7-B10, and the page's `useRef`/`useEffect` — and fix the pid branch, which is then decorative. If it's false, delete the *claim*, not the code. The verification named in the comment ("a dev-org verification that variant responses always include `variants[]`") is one API call; shipping a removal plan instead of doing it is the wrong trade at this size.

**3. `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:331-332, 336-337` vs `variantScopedPrice.ts:70-76` — Major — two comments in the same PR state opposite facts. CONFIRMED.**
Page: standalone variant "lacks tieredPrices reliably"; base ProductView's `getPriceData` "reads the standalone variant and **loses tieredPrices**". Module: Was/Now for colour+size "comes from the variant's own `tieredPrices` (**present** because we request `perPricebook:true`)… The active path for colour+size pricing is therefore the variant's own prices." One of these is wrong, and which one it is decides #1 and #2.

**4. `index.tsx:891-901` + `product-view/index.tsx:328-330, 590-597` — Major — the override is applied at the `renderHeader` boundary only, newly diverging the header price from Express Pay's amount. PLAUSIBLE.**
`ProductView` still computes `priceData = getPriceData(product, {quantity})` and feeds `priceData.currentPrice` to `SFPaymentsExpressButtons initialAmount`. Colour-only: header now shows the colour-scoped minimum, Express Pay keeps the master-wide minimum. Before this PR both came from the same object. Gated by `useExpressCheckoutEnabled().pdp`, so it may be dormant — but it's a conscious decision to record, not an accident. (`quantity` being dropped from the scoped call is benign: it only affects `tieredPrice`, which `selectPdpProductInfo` never reads.)

**5. `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:27-29` — Minor — the justification for the `baseStyle` stubs is factually false. CONFIRMED empirically.**
"omitting them would break variant application: Chakra gates variant resolution through the declared parts list." Chakra gates on `config.parts` (`@chakra-ui/styled-system/dist/index.js:1731,1740`), which is the `parts:` array on line 18 — not on `baseStyle`'s keys. I ran `resolveStyleConfig` against a real `toCSSVar(extendTheme({}))` theme with and without the stubs: byte-identical output (`{"container":{"margin":0,"display":"inline-flex"},"wasPrice":{"color":"RED"},"nowPrice":{"color":"GREEN"}}`). Removing the `parts` key entirely also changes nothing here. And no repo-wide invariant enforces it — `recipeGuards.test.ts` has no parts check, and `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:81-84` is scoped to `ZimmTextInput`. The stubs are harmless convention; the stated mechanism is not real.

**6. `index.tsx:357` — Minor — dead `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`. CONFIRMED.**
`npx eslint --report-unused-disable-directives overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` → `357:5 error Unused eslint-disable directive (no problems were reported from 'react-hooks/exhaustive-deps')`. `useRef` values are stable-known to the rule, so nothing was ever flagged. Beyond being dead, it misleads a reader into thinking the deps array is knowingly incomplete.

**7. `variantScopedPrice.ts:54-59` — Minor — the module's return type is `any`, so its careful input typing terminates in nothing. CONFIRMED.**
`getPriceData` resolves through the shorthand ambient declaration `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*';` (`overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts:171`) → `any`; there is no return annotation. `productInfo.ts:28-41` already declares exactly the subset consumed downstream (`PdpSourcePrice`). Annotating `: PdpSourcePrice | null` is the one genuinely missing link between the two modules — and would be the *only* type-level connection, since the page passes `product: SfccProduct` (= `any`, `index.tsx:107`) and `masterProductRef` is `useRef<SfccProduct|null>`, so `ScopedProduct`/`ScopedVariant` currently only bite inside the test file.

**8. `zimmProductName/zimmProductName.css.ts:6-7` and `zimmProductModelInfo/zimmProductModelInfo.css.ts:7` — Minor — sibling comments made false by this PR. CONFIRMED.**
Both read "Single-part, so no `parts` key and the component reads it through `useStyleConfig` — the same shape as `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` and `zimmProductDescription.css.ts`." `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` is now multi-part. Neither file is in the diff, but this PR is the cause; two-word fixes.

**9. `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:14-15` — Minor — dangling reference. CONFIRMED.**
"see the original single-part docblock for the full explanation" — that docblock lived in this same file on `develop` and was replaced by this PR. Nothing at HEAD contains it; the nearest surviving copy of the argument is `zimmProductName.css.ts:15-23`. Point there or inline the two sentences.

**10. `index.tsx:328` — Minor — comment cites a branch that doesn't exist. CONFIRMED.**
`(mirrors feature/SFCC-194_pdp-was-now-sale-price)`; the branch is `feature/SFCC-194_pdp-was-now-price` (`git branch -a`, `git ls-remote origin`). Branch names in shipped code rot at merge regardless — this belongs in the PR body.

**11. `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:90` — Minor — state-dependent styling leaked to JSX as `opacity={0}` while the component is already variant-driven.**
overrideStyling.md point 3 reserves the theme config for "anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state"; a `loading` variant would keep the one-canonical-styling-surface rule whole. Sibling precedent is explicit: `zimmProductName/index.tsx:29-30` — the element "carries no style prop of its own, so the recipe cannot be out-ranked by one." Everything else in this atom is correctly in the recipe. CONFIRMED against the rule.

**12. `index.tsx:338-365` — Minor — the React half of the extraction stayed inline.**
`useRef` + `useEffect` + `useMemo` + a derived flag added to a 999-line page. components.md's extract-to-hook threshold (a `useEffect` with a non-trivial dependency array, plus related state that changes together) points at `usePdpVariantScopedPrice(productResponse, product, urlParams) → {priceData, isPriceLoading}`. The pure part was extracted well; this is the remaining half.

**13. `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:21-28` — Minor — the messages are probably not extractable, contradicting the docblock. PLAUSIBLE.**
`extract-default-translations` runs bare `formatjs extract` with no `--additional-function-names` / `--extract-from-format-message-call` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/scripts/translations/extract-default-messages.js:39-45`), which does not pick up a hoisted object literal referenced by identifier. So "once it does [run], the non-English storefronts pick up their own strings with no change here" likely doesn't hold. `defineMessages({...})` makes it true for one import. Note this mirrors the pre-existing sibling `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:59` — a house-pattern issue, not a regression introduced here.

**14. Comment density — Minor — measured, and partly triplicated.**
`zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` 84 comment lines : 50 code; `variantScopedPrice.ts` 73 : 44; `staticProductHeader.tsx` 57 : 49. Much of it is genuinely load-bearing (the live-region rationale at `index.tsx:99-119` explains a real, non-obvious divergence from base and is worth every line). But the loading-placeholder/`opacity` rationale is stated three times — `index.tsx:82-87`, `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:51-55`, `index.test.tsx:113-114` — and the unreachability block (#2) is the single largest comment in the PR defending code that may not need to exist.

**15. `variantScopedPrice.ts:54-59` — Nit — signature design.** Four positional params with two adjacent `string | undefined` (`urlPid`, `urlColour`) — transposable with no type error, and `variantScopedPrice.test.ts` calls it positionally 14 times. `cachedMaster: ScopedProduct | null` vs `product: ScopedProduct | null | undefined` is inconsistent nullability. `variants?: ScopedVariant[]` could be `readonly` (typescript.md).

**16. Naming — Nit — three vocabularies for two values across one boundary.** Mapper emits `price`/`wasPrice` (`productInfo.ts:47-51`); molecule and atom take `currentPrice`/`originalPrice`; the atom's consts are `WAS_PRICE_MESSAGE`/`NOW_PRICE_MESSAGE`. They cross at `staticProductHeader.tsx:99-100` (`currentPrice={info.price}`, `originalPrice={info.wasPrice}`).

## What is genuinely well done

- **Layering is right.** Atom (presentation) → molecule (composition) → page-local selectors (`productInfo.ts` field mapping, `variantScopedPrice.ts` price selection) → page (data). No overlap between the two selectors — they're cleanly separated concerns, and there is **no duplication** between them (item 6: clean).
- **Container/presentational boundary holds.** No data-fetching below `pages/`. `StaticProductHeader`'s `useIntl` is the documented components.md exception and is justified at the site (`:33-39`), including the "throws without a Provider" caveat that the rule file itself calls out.
- **`variantScopedPrice.ts` is genuinely pure** — no hooks, no React, no side effects, deterministic, and mockable at exactly one seam. Extracting it was the right call and the page's memo really did reduce to one line.
- **The relative-vs-base-path import trap is handled and explained correctly** in both files that face it (`index.tsx:55-63`, `staticProductHeader.tsx:7-14`) — this is the exact hazard `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` warns about, and it's the rare case where a long comment is clearly earning its keep.
- **Token discipline is exact.** `minHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)'` is not a guess — `typography.ts:206` sets `price.lineHeight = lineHeights['2xs']` = 1.125rem, the same entry the var derives from. Every colour and gap is a `var(--zimm-*)`, no bare keys, no raw literals.
- **Tier/CODEOWNERS routing is correct for every file** (item 5): `ui-kits/**` → both squads (CODEOWNERS:176), co-located `*.css.ts` → both squads, no Tier 1/2 gate (CODEOWNERS:186, matching overrideStyling.md's co-location governance), `pages/product-detail/` → squad B (CODEOWNERS:162). Nothing Tier 1 touched; `theme/index.test.tsx` is a comment-only edit to a non-frozen file.
- **Minimal changes hold** (item 7). Nothing off-ticket in source. The only noise is the generated `.claude/registry/*` churn (Header 13→1, Link 25→35 consumer counts), which is baseline-regeneration artefact and hook-mandated, not authored.
- **TypeScript** (item 4): no new `any` — the `SfccProduct`/`SfccVariant` aliases are pre-existing at `index.tsx:95-109` with a documented deferral and an identified replacement (`ShopperProductsTypes.Product`). `ProductViewHeaderProps & { isPriceLoading?: boolean }` is the right utility-type move. No `as` casts added, `satisfies SystemStyleObject` used throughout, `import type` correct. The one gap is #7.

## Verdict

Not blocked on style, structure, or tiering — the atom/molecule/mapper/page split is correct, token and TypeScript discipline are above this repo's average, and the extraction was worth doing.

It **is** blocked on one substantive thing: findings #1/#2/#3 are three views of a single unresolved question — does an SFCC variant response carry `variants[]`? — and the PR currently ships mutually contradictory answers to it, with a documented mitigation (the stale-pid guard) that is inert under one of them. That's a five-minute dev-org check, then a small edit either way.

Fix #1-#3 plus the cheap corrections (#5, #6, #9, #10 are all one-liners); #4 needs a recorded decision; the rest are follow-up-grade.
